name: Antwork Field Code for ACF & SCF
author: Antwork

sections.description:
Antwork Field Code is a code generator for Advanced Custom Fields and Secure Custom Fields. It adds a “Field Code” box under the settings of each field group, with the snippets that display the fields of the saved group in a theme template: the code of each covered field, chosen in the list of fields, coloured by WordPress’s own code editor, with a Copy button.

The code follows the documentation of Advanced Custom Fields: get_field() returns values that are not escaped, so every value is escaped for where it is printed (esc_html(), esc_url(), esc_attr(), wp_kses_post(), wp_get_attachment_image() for images), and nothing is printed when a field is empty. It follows the WordPress Coding Standards, runs on PHP 7.4 to 8.4, and names its variables after your fields.

It works with Advanced Custom Fields (free or Pro, version 6) and with Secure Custom Fields.

Features

  • Code for each covered field: choose a field in the list, in the order of the field group, to see its code, read only. It reads your field group as it is saved, with the settings that change the code: return format (value, label or array; object or ID; URL…), one or several values, appearance of taxonomy fields, new lines of text areas, tabs of icon pickers.
  • Copy: a Copy button for each field and “Copy all” for the whole group. Copying is announced to screen readers and works with the keyboard.
  • Field list: pick a field, or All fields for the whole template; the arrow keys move between fields.
  • Group fields: the sub-fields of a Group field are read from the group’s value, at any depth.
  • Readable code: one variable per field, a guard on empty values, comments where a value needs explaining (formatted dates, post objects or IDs).
  • Help menu: links to the support forum and to the reviews on WordPress.org, and a button that copies your WordPress, PHP, ACF or SCF and plugin versions to the clipboard (shown to users who can see Site Health). Nothing is sent from your site.
  • For developers: filters let another plugin cover a field type, add a location (such as an options page), and add code before or after each snippet.

Covered field types

  • Basic: Text, Text Area, Number, Range, Email, URL, Password (read, never printed).
  • Content: Image (Array, URL, ID), File (Array, URL, ID), Wysiwyg Editor, oEmbed.
  • Choice: Select (one or several values; Value, Label or Array), Checkbox, Radio Button and Button Group (Value, Label or Array), True / False.
  • Relational: Link (Array or URL), Post Object (one or several; Post Object or Post ID), Page Link (one or several), Relationship (Post Object or Post ID), Taxonomy (Checkbox, Multi Select, Radio Buttons or Select; Term Object or Term ID), User (one or several; User Array, User Object or User ID).
  • Advanced: Google Map, Date Picker, Date Time Picker, Time Picker, Color Picker (Hex string, RGBA string or RGBA array), Icon Picker (String or Array).
  • Layout: Group, with its sub-fields. Message, Tab, Accordion and Separator hold no value and get no code.

Repeater, Flexible Content, Gallery, Clone and field types added by other plugins show “This field type is not covered yet.”

Where the code works

The code reads the fields of the current post, inside the Loop of a template for posts, pages or custom post types. A field group shown elsewhere (an options page, a taxonomy, a user, ACF Blocks…) still gets its code, with a line that names the location that is not covered yet.

Antwork Field Code Pro

Antwork Field Code Pro is a separate plugin, sold at antwork.fr. It adds the code of Repeater, Flexible Content, Gallery and Clone fields, and of field groups shown on options pages, taxonomy terms, users, comments, attachments and widgets. Where it would apply, the Field Code box says so in one sentence that you can dismiss.

Ideas and bugs

Have an idea for the plugin? Suggest it in the support forum, where bugs are reported too.

Privacy

Privacy: this plugin makes no external request. It collects no data, adds no tracking and stores no option in the database, so there is nothing to clean up when you delete it.

Antwork Field Code is an independent plugin. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Advanced Custom Fields or Secure Custom Fields.

If it saves you time, a review on WordPress.org helps other developers find it.

Switching from another code generator

The code appears under the settings of each field group.

  1. Deactivate the other code generator, if any.
  2. Install and activate Antwork Field Code.
  3. Edit a field group: the “Field Code” box shows the code of its fields.

There is nothing to set up and nothing to migrate: the plugin stores no settings.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Advanced Custom Fields or Secure Custom Fields.
  2. Install Antwork Field Code from the Plugins screen (Plugins > Add New, search for “Antwork Field Code”) and activate it.
  3. Edit a field group and save it: the “Field Code” box appears under its settings.
  4. Copy the code of a field, or “Copy all”, and paste it into a template of your theme (for example single.php), inside the Loop.
sections.faq:
Does it need Advanced Custom Fields?

It needs Advanced Custom Fields (free or Pro, version 6) or Secure Custom Fields. Without one of them, it only shows a notice on the Plugins screen and does nothing else.

Who sees the Field Code box?

The users who may manage field groups: by default, administrators (the capability set for Advanced Custom Fields or Secure Custom Fields, manage_options unless changed).

Why does the box ask me to save the field group?

The code is built from the saved field group, on the server. Save the field group after adding or changing fields to see their code.

Is the code safe to paste in my theme?

Yes: every value is escaped for where it is printed, as the documentation of Advanced Custom Fields recommends. Text goes through esc_html(), links through esc_url(), attributes through esc_attr(), HTML content (Wysiwyg, Text Area with new lines) through wp_kses_post(), images through wp_get_attachment_image(), and the oEmbed field keeps its iframe only. Field names are written as plain PHP strings, so an unusual field name cannot break the code.

Why is my field type not covered?

Repeater, Flexible Content, Gallery and Clone fields are covered by Antwork Field Code Pro, a separate plugin. The field types of other plugins are not covered yet: tell us which one you need in the support forum.

Does it change my field groups or my database?

No. It reads the field group and shows code. It writes nothing in the database, makes no external request and stores no settings.

Can another plugin change the code?

Yes. The filters awfc_field_renderers (cover or replace a field type), awfc_locations (add a location, such as an options page, with the post ID it passes to get_field()), awfc_location_post_id (change that post ID with the whole location rule), awfc_snippet_header and awfc_snippet_footer (add code before or after each snippet) are documented in the plugin’s repository.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • The sub-fields of a Group field tell other plugins which array they are read from (container), and the new filter awfc_location_post_id receives the whole location rule, such as the options page.
  • A field named args is read into $args_field, so that it never replaces the $args of a widget.
  • Under a field type or a location that Antwork Field Code Pro covers, the Field Code box says so in one sentence, with a link and a Dismiss button. Dismissing is remembered in your browser: nothing is stored on your site and no request is made.

1.0.0

  • First release: the code of 29 field types, with each return format and appearance, escaped as the ACF documentation recommends; Copy, Copy all and field list; help menu; hooks for field types, locations, headers and footers.
